methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $12M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Salient Motion is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company operating in the same sector, including later-stage companies such as Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $12M raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $24M. Peer-median analysis examines the four sampled robotics and manufacturing companies across adjacent stages, producing a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The peer-based method reflects a portfolio of companies at Series B maturity and one seed-stage outlier, creating significant stage-adjusted dispersion.

The triangulated range spans $20M (floor) to $2.0B (ceiling), with a median of $862M. The wide band reflects the methodological gap between early-stage funding progression and later-stage peer medians. Key uncertainties include stage-adjustment discount applicable to a Series A relative to Series B comparables, revenue traction not specified in the data, and the relevance of the seed-stage Walden peer to valuation anchoring. Stage-adjusted pricing likely falls materially below the peer median.
